text: player
Natsuki Shinomiya
I'm telling you, it's true... Why won't you believe me?!
Just last night, I saw green flames in the classroom!
Undoubtedly, a will-o'-the-wisp – a gathering of restless souls... No, that's not quite right. "Spectral fire"... yes, that's a better term for it.
Is there even a difference?
Green flames... It's certainly a bit strange, isn't it?
Mirai
Just calm down a little bit. Where exactly did you see it? Don't tell me it was in the lab building...
Green flames... That's probably copper burning.
Yui Yagi
Flame test.
A familiar voice comes from behind. I turn around, and, as expected, it's Yui Yagi.
Come to think of it, she seldom talks outside of mahjong and seems somewhat nervous now.
Ah – ahh! So it's just a flame test thing!
That's the one! It's discovered by that famous professor... What's his name again?
Isn't the flame test from junior high textbooks?
Oh... Is... is that so?
Electrons in metals absorb energy when heated, and jump to unstable higher energy levels.
After that, they spontaneously fall back to lower energy levels, releasing photons of different energies...
Right – those photons correspond to wavelengths of light, which is why the flame changes color!
That's our Yui! Spot-on, just like usual.
Wait... was this also covered in junior high?
...Nah, no way they taught the actual theory in junior high.
As we keep joking around, Yui and Mirai suddenly click – their scientific discussion grows more intense and technical by the second.
Professional terms we'd never even heard before come flying out one after another, leaving absolutely no room for the rest of us to get a word in.
At this rate, Natsuki and I are about to fade into the background like NPCs... What should we do?
Hey, since there are four of us now... wanna go play some mahjong?
Mahjong? I'd love to... but not today.
I've got an invention symposium I have to attend – oh shoot, it's almost time! Gotta go now!
Ah, I should probably head out too – got my shift at the bar starting soon. Sorry, guys!
Oh... what a shame. Guess we'll have to wait for next time, then...
Uh... so...
And just like that, only Yui and I stay.
How about we just call it here?
Under the weight of that awkward silence, Yui doesn't say a word. She just looks at me.
Her expression remains as unreadable as ever – those eyes give away nothing.
Does she not want to leave yet? Guess it's up to me to break the ice...
It seems that you are really into science.
Is there something on my face?
...Not really sure about that.
Huh? What does that mean?
Since my parents are scientists, I've been reading science books since I was little.
But... you know so much about everything...
That's why I thought you were into science.
...Is that so?
...If you say it like that, then I guess maybe I do.
If you don't want to be a scientist... then what do you want to be?
Well...?
...Right. What do I want to do?
...What kind of person do I truly want to become...?
Eh? Is that too deep...? Sorry! You don't really need to take it that seriously!
I just wanted to make some small talk...
But Yui turned serious... She seems genuinely troubled by my words.
Not good – better change the subject fast...
Science aside, there are plenty of other things we can talk about.
...Mhm. Thank you, senpai.
Yui remains silent, her gaze still locked onto me.
Wait... could my offhand remark actually be right? Gotta wipe my face just to check.
...You guessed right, senpai.
Eh? Is there really something on my face?
Yes, it's the look on your face... quite amusing to observe.
If you don't like me doing that, I'll stop. Sorry.
It's... not that I don't like it...
Eh... You find observing me that interesting?
After all, by every possible measure, I'm just... thoroughly average in One Han City.
...Your reactions are kind of fascinating.
Senpai, you really should be more aware of your own interesting side.
Wait... are you teasing me?
I'm telling the truth.
Is... that so...
Usually, someone with Yui's personality should be the more interesting one...
We should be heading the same way home, right?
I've seen you at the convenience store near my place before. So I figured we must live close by.
Really? I didn't even notice...
But even if we're not, I'd be happy to walk you home today.
Mmhm.
Do you usually cook at home, Yui?
Yeah. Still practicing, though.
Then let's hit the supermarket on the way. I need to grab a few things too.
Afterward, we head to the supermarket nearby.
It's a well-stocked supermarket, so we should be able to find everything we need.
Mm... I'm out of milk too. Might as well grab some while we're here.
What are you planning to make tonight, Yui?
Wait, don't tell me. Let me take a guess.
The ingredients in her shopping basket should give away what she's planning to make.
Let me see... Lettuce, kale, romaine, red leaf lettuce...?
Green cabbage, red cabbage, savoy cabbage...
Mm... Yui...
Seriously, what are you gonna do with all these leafy greens?
Didn't you just say you're gonna take a guess?
Could it be... some kind of hodgepodge!
Is it that you have a pet rabbit?
Wrong answer.
Is it that hard to guess?
Well... pretty hard.
So... what's the answer?
Beef and potato stew.
Huh?
Then... what about the potatoes?
Technically, you don't have to put potatoes in beef and potato stew.
Only by daring to try new ingredients can we forge new paths in cuisine... Probably.
But... if you don't add potatoes, it's not even beef and potato stew anymore...
Why do I feel like that she's innovating in the wrong direction...
Wait... does this mean you can't actually cook...?
...See? You really are interesting.
Though I've never had a pet.
Is that so... I saw your basket was full of veggies, so I thought...
The correct answer is beef and potato stew.
Also, feeding rabbits too many veggies can be dangerous.
Veggies are mainly for hydration, so you should only give them a tiny amount. 3 grams per kilogram of their weight is the absolute maximum.
Hold up! Don't think I didn't hear that terrifying "correct" answer just now!
Actually, for rabbits, hay is far more nutritious than fresh vegetables.
Senpai, don't you find it amazing?
Uh... you're derailing the conversation hard.
How are you gonna make beef and potato stew with these?
You have to dare to break the old rules sometimes.
Look, potatoes in beef and potato stew isn't a "rule" – it's literally in the name!
Waaah...
A child's crying echoes from nearby.
Looking around, a little girl – about four or five years old – stands in front of the bakery display, looking utterly lost.
...Could she have gotten separated from her family?
Since it's a weekday afternoon, there are barely any customers in the supermarket, and no staff nearby either.
(Well... Should we go help?)
...Let's go check on her.
Yui strides ahead of me, swiftly walking over to the little girl.
She crouches down to meet the little girl eye to eye, her voice softening as she gently asks what's wrong.
What happened to you?
Did you get separated from your mommy and daddy?
Little Girl
...Sniffle.
Mommy... Where's Mommy...?
It's okay.
We'll help you find her.
There's no customer service desk on this floor...
Senpai, you'll help too, right?
Sure, we'll help you find your mommy together.
Thank you...
So, do you remember where you last saw her?
I was looking at the bubble guns earlier...
I kept looking... and then Mommy was gone.
So... what's the best way to handle this?
Let's go check the second floor.
Let's wait near the exit.
This should be where she got separated from her mom.
We've searched around the toy shelves but haven't seen anyone who looks like her mother...
If her mom's also looking for her, she might have already gone somewhere else, right?
Mommy...
Where did Mommy go...?
Tears well up in the little girl's eyes again... This is bad. We're completely clueless about what to do.
Perhaps it would be better to ask a staff member to help?
At the very least, we should be able to use the store's PA system – it's better than nothing...
Don't worry, we'll find her for sure.
Unlike my panicked self, Yui remains as calmly composed as ever. And for some reason, there's an unusual gentleness about her now.
She crouches beside the little girl again, gently stroking her hair.
Do you know why soapy water can blow perfectly round bubbles?
And why plain water can't do the same?
Sniff... sniffle...
Sniffle... I don't know...
...How did we get onto blowing bubbles?
Imagine that we have a cup filled with water.
The water in the cup is actually made up of countless tiny particles.
We call them "molecules."
What... what does that mean...
...Sorry. Let me put it in simpler terms.
Alright...
...Little fairies.
There are many, many little fairies living in the water in the cup.
Of course, it's just a metaphor. Little fairies aren't real – it's just to simplify the explanation.
That's right, Yui! The fairies explanation is perfect!
No need to explain that part...
...I see.
Little fairies? ...Are they even smaller than me?
Yes, they're so tiny that we can't even see them.
But you know – those little fairies work really hard.
They hold each other's hands so hard, trying to keep the water from scattering into a puddle.
And so, they form a sphere, because that's the most stable shape.
Now we need to talk about the concept of surface tension, because surfactants weaken the cohesion between water molecules...
Yui, you're going too far again!
This is so tough...
The little girl probably doesn't understand a single word of Yui's explanation.
Yet somehow, her tears have stopped, replaced now by a soft smile.
Perhaps it's the focus in Yui's explanation that is drawing her in.
Also... maybe it's just my imagination, but now her eyes are glowing with pure curiosity.
I get it now!
The soap bubbles are round because the fairies are holding hands!
That's right...!
Yui clears her throat, then gently pats the girl's head.
So, until we find your mom... let's hold our hands, okay?
As long as we work together like the little fairies in the water, we'll definitely find her!
Although Yui seems a little embarrassed saying this, I think it's remarkable that she managed to say it out loud.
I thought she wasn't great with people... but maybe I just didn't know her well enough.
Yui takes the little girl's hand and walks ahead of me. Watching their backs, I feel a sudden warmth in my chest.
...Ellie? Is that you?
An anxious voice calls out from behind us.
We turn around and see a long-haired woman standing at the escalator landing.
The little girl dashes toward her with pure joy – finally, a mother-daughter reunion.
Little Girl's Mother
Thank you so much, both of you! Ellie, come say thank you too!
Thank you for helping me find Mommy!
Don't get lost again, okay? Be careful next time.
Okay! I will!
Yui waves goodbye to the mother and daughter, and the corners of her eyes seem to crinkle, just a little...
Is she... smiling?
Now that I think about it... even though her facial muscles barely move, if you look closely, her emotions show through.
...This is quite the discovery.
...I'm so glad we found her.
Yeah, and it's all thanks to you.
It's because you treated that little girl with kindness that she was willing to come with us.
I only did that... for myself.
Looking at that little girl, it was like seeing my past self.
Your past self?
Hm? What is it?
I forgot there's a delivery coming today.
Eh? When would that be?
Between 4 and 6 PM. It should be arriving any minute now.
I check my phone. It's 20 minutes left until 5 PM.
Uh... what do we do? Can you still make it?
Sorry, senpai. I have to head back home now.
Sure, be safe on your way!
You too.
Yui has just sprinted a few meters when she suddenly stops and turns back.
At this moment, her expression is still a bit hard for me to read.
It's been a fun day.
See you at the mahjong table, senpai.
The way she's standing... It's like she's reluctant to leave.
Hope it's not just me overthinking.
Rather than searching aimlessly, why don't we wait at a spot where her mother is sure to pass by?
Brilliant strategy...!
Although it's a bit exaggerated, being praised by Yui feels pretty good.
Once the little girl calms down, we guide her toward the supermarket exit.
As I expected, the little girl's mother appears before us shortly after.
Mommy! Where have you been?!
Ellie suddenly disappeared, so Mommy was looking for you...
Ah, are we having curry tonight?
Eh? I guess we are?
That's just how kids are, switching topics so fast that even her mom can't keep up... Before leaving, the little girl's mother gave us her sincere thanks.
After waving goodbye to the little girl, Yui murmurs something beside me.
I'm thinking about curry too.
Now that you mention it...
But the ingredients you bought won't work for curry, right? Should we head back to the fresh produce section?
Hm? Didn't we already buy all the ingredients?
It's common knowledge that beef stew with potatoes and curry basically use the same ingredients.
...I don't even know where to begin...
Regardless, Yui seems determined to make curry tonight, so we head to the spice aisle.
Uh, Yui, you're not thinking of making the spices yourself, are you?
Maybe we should try store-bought curry powder or roux first...?
Wait, you really don't need chili bean sauce in curry! Just put that down first!
...So I only add it after mastering curry techniques?
Not really... How should I put it, at least the concept of curry doesn't include...
Oh right. Senpai, next time we play mahjong, I'll bring you my homemade curry.
Ah, hmm... I'll look forward to it.
Yui's face remains expressionless – but as she meticulously selects spices, I can almost sense a hint of joy.
...But when I think about what comes next...
I can't really say I'm feeling joyful as well...
Did you say something?
N-no, nothing!
Our Ordinary Days
Activity Room, National University of Fuuchi
Well, that's something you can figure out later, one step at a time.
Ah, I just remembered, my fridge is empty...
Bubble guns... should be in the toy aisle. Is it on the second floor?
We take the little girl to the second floor.
However... I don't actually want to become a scientist myself. I'm probably different from those who genuinely love science.
